# Public syntax/build checks
The external public evaluator parses Python/JavaScript/Vue/TypeScript source or checks Go/PHP/Ruby syntax / compiles public Java sources. These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior. Preserve original TASK and public README/source obligations. Independent training Oracle also applies; do not access its implementation or references. No hidden schedules or assertions are included.

public_inputs.task:
# Task

The preparation service can now report that a file is still pending before it becomes ready. Update the file download dialog so it keeps checking pending preparation and delivers the file only after a ready status.

limitations: Only TASK and supplied public source/documents establish requirements; experiences, automatic contracts, and evaluation observations remain fallible guidance.
Attempt 1 passed syntax and acceptance checks, but no behavioral observations establish causality, completeness, or cross-task effectiveness.
Retry delay, backoff, maximum attempts, transport failure handling, and undocumented statuses are unspecified.
The scheduler and cancellation hooks do not document inline invocation, reentry, or cancellation guarantees; related checks are defensive preservation guidance.
The supplied implementation represents delivery through completed tokens; no separate file-transfer API is supplied.

rules.body: Apply when asynchronous preparation can remain pending and an existing run identity distinguishes replacement work. TASK: "The preparation service can now report that a file is still pending before it becomes ready. Update the file download dialog so it keeps checking pending preparation and delivers the file only after a ready status." Original src/usePreparation.js establishes run identity with "lifecycle.current.generation += 1;" and rejects obsolete results with "if (lifecycle.current.disposed || generation !== lifecycle.current.generation) return;".

Continue documented pending results through the existing retry scheduler, retaining the originating generation. Validate that generation and disposal state before retry execution initiates another check and before a result schedules continuation or records completion. Equal tokens do not distinguish successive runs: src/usePreparation.js uses "check(beginGeneration());" in both start and reopen. Cancellation of a handle complements these validity checks; it does not establish that an already issued result or callback cannot arrive.

Derive invalidation from each surface's existing ownership policy. src/DownloadDialog.jsx supplies "const preparation = usePreparation(token, { invalidateOnClose: true });"; src/usePreparation.js closes with "if (invalidateOnClose) beginGeneration();" and unmounts with "lifecycle.current.disposed = true;\n    beginGeneration();". In contrast, src/useBackgroundPreparation.js states "// Closing this progress panel does not cancel workspace-owned work." Preserve that distinction. Do not import shared-cache restoration, queue record fields, stream cleanup, form readiness, network modes or focus gates from unrelated experiences.

- Only TASK and supplied public source/documents establish requirements. Experiences, automatic contracts and evaluation observations remain fallible guidance.
- Attempt 1 reports syntax checks and acceptance passing, with no behavioral observations. This does not establish causality, completeness or cross-task effectiveness.
- Retry delay, backoff, maximum attempts, transport failure handling and undocumented statuses are unspecified.
- The scheduler and cancellation hooks do not document inline invocation, reentry or cancellation guarantees. Checks around these boundaries are defensive preservation guidance, not evidence that such behavior occurs.
- The supplied implementation represents completion through completed tokens; no separate file-transfer API is supplied.
- This reflection modifies no files and accesses no scorer, reference implementation or hidden tests.

Check successive PENDING results followed by READY: each current retry starts another check, loading remains active until READY, and completion retains token deduplication. Separately release old results and cancelled callbacks after close, unmount, replacement start and same-token reopen; they must not initiate checks, schedule continuation or mutate replacement state. Check initial transport entry remains immediate, current retry state and handle ownership remain coherent, and background preparation continues after its panel closes. If exercising inline scheduler invocation or cancellation reentry, treat these as defensive boundary probes rather than documented business schedules. VISIBLE_CHECKS.md states: "These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior."

checkpoints: On start, the dialog immediately begins a check for the current token, sets loading true, increments checkCount, and publishes a snapshot.
For the current generation, every PENDING result schedules a later retry through schedulePreparationRetry; the retry revalidates lifecycle authority before starting another check.
A PENDING result does not add the token to completed and does not end loading.
A READY result for the current generation ends loading and adds the originating request token to completed at most once.
Close, reopen, a replacement start, and unmount invalidate foreground work and cancel any owned scheduled retry so stale responses or callbacks cannot check, complete, or publish.
Closing BackgroundExportPanel only hides it; workspace-owned preparation continues until owner disposal.
snapshot returns a new completed array rather than exposing the internal mutable array.
forbidden_effects: Do not deliver or record a file as completed for PENDING.
Do not let a response or retry from an invalidated generation affect a replacement foreground run, including when the token value is reused.
Do not let foreground close or unmount leave an owned retry active.
Do not convert retry scheduling into immediate recursive polling or invent a retry delay, retry limit, backoff, or timeout.
Do not change background-panel close into cancellation of workspace-owned preparation.
Do not mutate tests, configuration, dependencies, public commands, or unrelated behavior.
lifecycle_identity: Foreground authority is the combination of the captured request token and the generation returned by beginGeneration().
Each foreground response and retry belongs to its originating generation; token equality alone does not authorize work after close, restart, or reopen.
The disposed flag is the terminal owner boundary and forbids subsequent foreground publication or continuation.
Background preparation has a distinct owner lifetime represented by active; panel visibility is not its cancellation identity.

obligations.text: The file download dialog must continue checking when the preparation service reports PENDING and must deliver or record completion only after READY.
Each PENDING result belonging to the current foreground generation must schedule another check through the supplied retry scheduler while loading remains active.
A READY result belonging to the current foreground generation must stop loading and add its captured request token to completed without duplicates.

Foreground close, replacement start, reopen, and unmount must invalidate obsolete continuations and cancel their owned scheduled retry; stale responses and callbacks must not check, complete, or publish.
Existing immediate start behavior, state fields, check counting, visibility behavior, snapshot isolation, and public imperative commands must be preserved.
Background preparation ownership must remain separate: hiding its panel must not cancel workspace-owned work, while unmount must release its retry resources.

ordering_barriers: Capture the foreground generation and request token before issuing each transport check.
After each transport resolution, verify that the hook is not disposed and that the captured generation is still current before interpreting the status or scheduling continuation.
Before a scheduled retry initiates transport work, verify that its originating generation is still current and the hook is not disposed.
Invalidate the old generation and cancel its owned retry before beginning replacement foreground work.
For READY, validate lifecycle authority before changing loading, completed, or rendered state.
Unmount marks the foreground owner disposed before generation invalidation and cleanup.
preservation: Preserve direct initial checking from start and reopen rather than deferring the first check to the retry scheduler.
Preserve visible, loading, retryScheduled, checkCount, completed, and token snapshot fields and their existing meanings.
Preserve completed-token deduplication and copying in snapshot().
Preserve BackgroundExportPanel's independent workspace-owned lifetime and close-as-hide behavior.
Preserve the injected preparation transport, retry scheduler, and cancellation interfaces.
scope: Business code for the foreground file-download preparation flow in src/usePreparation.js and its existing use by src/DownloadDialog.jsx.
The public status, scheduling, and cancellation boundary in src/preparation-api.js.
Adjacent background preparation is in preservation scope only; the task does not request changing its ownership policy.

rules.body: The current source retains a history or audit effect for admitted work after navigation, while UI publication belongs to its originating visit. Decoding may complete immediately or after suspension.

Capture admission identity, including visit and attempt where present. Complete the retained audit according to its cardinality contract; then recheck the originating visit immediately before visible publication. Recheck after callback-capable auditing because it may navigate.

Listener removal, a newer display and old-view retirement do not retract an already admitted retained effect. Preserve its original identity and required count, suppress retired-visit painting and keep the current visit's valid delivery live.

Do not use one early eligibility check for both audit and display. Retained audit never authorizes stale UI publication. If the current source explicitly revokes or discards history, follow that policy rather than imposing retention.

Complete admitted work after hide, switch, cancellation/retry where supported, disposal and same-source reopening. Check audit count and identity separately from display; navigate inside the audit callback and verify publication permission is checked again.

rules.body: Apply when preparation reports pending repeatedly, the client owns retries, and foreground presentation and background preparation have separate lifetimes. TASK states: "Update the foreground preparation client so it keeps checking pending preparation and delivers the package only after a ready status." README.md states: "The transport asynchronously fulfills false (pending) or true (ready). It can\nreport pending repeatedly. It does not issue retries itself."

Treat pending as a continuation of preparation. Schedule another check after every pending response until readiness or lifecycle invalidation; pending must not record or deliver completion. Preserve the existing ready-only completion branch in src/workflow.py: "if ready is True:" and its duplicate prevention: "if token not in self.state['completed']:self.state['completed'].append(token)".

Reuse the existing cancellable scheduling boundary for retries while preserving immediate initial check entry and asynchronous future notification. README.md states: "Retry callbacks are\nscheduled for a later event turn and can be cancelled; no real-time interval is\npart of this API." src/workflow.py states: "# Host futures notify through the asyncio loop; timers are injected separately." Do not replace scheduling with immediate recursive polling or invent a required retry interval.

Keep each response bound to its captured token and generation. Check lifecycle authority before response effects and queued retry work. src/workflow.py captures "token=self.state['token']" and guards both callbacks with "if self.disposed or generation!=self.generation:return". Preserve invalidation and retry cancellation on foreground start, reopen, close and owner disposal so obsolete work cannot publish, complete or check for a replacement lifecycle.

Keep foreground closure separate from workspace ownership. README.md states: "The adjacent workspace job has its own\nlifetime; its panel is only a display. Final owner disposal releases resources." Preserve WorkspaceJob preparation after panel closure and resource release on disposal; do not propagate foreground cancellation policy into workspace close.

Preserve public commands, token identity, check counting, unique completed tokens and snapshot isolation. src/workflow.py copies completion state with "return dict(self.state,completed=list(self.state['completed']))". Reuse existing completion and scheduling behavior without changing tests, configuration, dependencies or unrelated resource policy.

Not specified in this candidate.

- The verdict difference does not establish that clearing loading during pending caused failure. TASK and public documentation do not explicitly prescribe loading presentation between checks.

Check completed-list snapshot isolation, duplicate prevention, check counts, workspace continuation after panel close and disposal cleanup.

rules.body: View subscriptions define document filtering, event payloads and retirement notifications. Historical cases include both removal before saving and preserving a departing view's opportunity to receive its save status.

Preserve document reads and presentation, original event payloads and filtering. If the host requires the departing view to receive this save notification, deliver it in that order before removal. If retirement immediately forbids UI effects, mark invalidity first and protect later output.
Preserve public and injected interfaces, exact text, store-generated status and revision semantics, and normal subscription release.
Do not force different cases' notification contracts into one cleanup order. Checking stored values alone can miss status-display regressions and subscription leaks.
Observe notification-versus-detachment order, events after retirement, filtering of other documents, reads on reopening, and document/status output after nested navigation.

rules.body: A deferred result can arrive after terminal close/dispose of its originating modal. Operation invocation/completion and an application-shell or other consumer have independent lifetimes.

Check that originating modal's current closed state in the completion continuation, before assigning its value or emitting a write. An admission-time snapshot is insufficient, including closure during notify. Preserve result acquisition, assignment, write and any existing publication in their original synchronous order. Where an existing publication follows a callback-capable write, a post-write closure check protects that publication; apply it only to that source's existing effect.

Keep notify invocation and original-payload completion/returned delivery outside the modal-effect guard, including calls made after close. Closing suppresses modal mutation/write/publication, not the independent operation result. Preserve value and payload identity, snapshot shape, controller verbs, terminal closure, separate modal instances, actual unmount cleanup and the existing disposeChild behavior.

Limit the repair to the modal subscription; preserve shell independence without inventing its implementation. Do not add publication where absent, defer callbacks, impose freshness/request supersession, add cancellation or import persistent-buffer policies. Post-write reentry is a conditional defensive checkpoint, not a universal host guarantee. Rejection handling, callback exceptions, additional disposeChild semantics and concurrent-result ordering remain unspecified unless current source supplies them.

Check completion while open, after close, after dispose, during notify closure, run after close, multiple completions and actual unmount cleanup. Observe modal value, write, any existing publication and returned payload separately. Check unchanged disposeChild, independent instances and shell policy. Where writes can reenter closure and publication exists, verify no subsequent publication but continued original-result delivery. Syntax/acceptance alone does not prove behavioral completeness or causality.

rules.body:
Apply when a shared progress source serves distinct visits and attempts, startup can emit synchronously, full-frame decoding may finish later, and history and presentation have different lifetimes. README.md: "Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit." README.md: "The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order." Confirm these premises and the target's display-order requirement before applying freshness suppression.

Register panel reception before invoking startup, preserving later streaming. Original src/workflow.go: "env.Call("start",file.Token);subscription=env.Call("listen",file.Token,callback)". TASK: "Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior." Make retirement effective during startup so subsequent packets cannot start new work through an obsolete subscription, even before the outer startup returns. Keep already admitted decoding separate from that admission decision.

When the task requires full-frame freshness, assign ordering at packet reception before decoding or callback-capable work. Scope ordering to the display owner, including attempts sharing one visit. After a newer frame has been published, suppress older frames only from presentation. Recheck both visit authority and publication order after audit callbacks; commit the publication watermark before calling the display sink, which may reenter delivery. TASK: "Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward." README.md: "A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset." Reception order, rather than loaded magnitude or completion order, determines freshness. Buffering every result until arrival order can be reconstructed is not required.

Keep audit completion independent of display permission. Capture the originating file, attempt and visit; retain the existing audit effect for each admitted decode, including completion after hide, replacement, cancellation or disposal. Audit before deciding whether to paint, then recheck visit authority and freshness because audit may synchronously navigate or complete another decode. README.md: "recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel." Original src/workflow.go: "deliver:=func(frame interface{}){;audit(frame);view(frame,order)}". A stale display frame still retains its history effect.

Coordinate ownership across callback-capable startup and cleanup. Publish cleanup ownership before startup callbacks can navigate; reconcile the returned handle without overwriting resources installed by newer navigation. Remove old resources from current ownership before canceling them, and recheck the navigation request after cleanup returns. Cancel captured retired resources and preserve repeated cleanup behavior.
